6.meaning: And the believing women — women who have faith, who trust and affirm the truth. The feminine counterpart of 'mu'minūn' (believing men); a participle from 'to believe, to have faith.'
6.grammar: A feminine plural active participle ('believing women / the women who believe'), made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is the subject (nominative) form for the sound feminine plural, marking the women as the ones spoken about or doing the action.
6.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, to trust; faith, security

7.meaning: 'Against / with themselves' or 'by means of themselves.' Combines the preposition bi- ('with/against/by') with 'anfus' ('selves, souls', the plural of nafs) and a possessive 'their'.
7.grammar: 'Anfus' is the broken plural of 'nafs' (self/soul). The preposition bi- governs the genitive case, shown by the -i vowel before the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The whole phrase functions adverbially ('with/against their own selves').
7.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; the inner being

8.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
8.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

9.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
9.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

10.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

11.meaning: A noun, 'a fabrication, a brazen falsehood, a slanderous lie' — a statement deliberately invented and turned away from the truth.
11.grammar: A noun. The -un ending marks the nominative and indefinite case ('a lie'), the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('it is a fabrication'). The root sense is of something 'turned' away from reality.
11.root: أ-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — to turn away (from truth), fabricate, lie

12.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
12.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
1.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: They came — the act of coming or arriving, attributed to a group ('they').
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-ū' marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), denoting a completed act of arriving carried out by a group.

3.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
3.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

4.meaning: "With four (of...)" — the numeral four preceded by the preposition bi- 'with/by means of'; built to be completed by a following counted noun ('four of ...').
4.grammar: bi- is the preposition 'with/by'. The final -i is the genitive case, which a noun must take after a preposition; it also signals that the number links forward to a following noun ('four OF ...'). Arabic numbers 3-10 take the tā' marbūṭa ending when counting masculine nouns — the 'reverse agreement' rule.

5.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
5.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
5.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

6.meaning: Then when
6.grammar: A noun in context, taking the case required by its syntactic role.

7.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

7.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

8.meaning: They come / they bring / they will come — a verb meaning that they approach, arrive, or present something.
8.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ū plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they.' The stem keeps the root's hamza (written on the alif seat). The shortened -ū form (rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in a dependent (subjunctive/jussive) mood, the form taken after certain particles.

9.meaning: 'With the witnesses' — shuhadāʾ is the plural of shahīd, one who bears witness; the word denotes those who can attest firsthand to the truth of a matter.
9.grammar: bi- is the preposition 'with/by'; al- is 'the' (its l merges into the following sh in pronunciation). The final -i is the genitive ending, which every noun takes after a preposition; it can also link a noun to a preceding one as '...OF...'.

10.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
11.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

14.meaning: The liars — those who habitually speak falsehood, a definite group of males or a mixed group. The base denotes lying and untruthfulness.
14.grammar: The definite article plus an active participle (a 'doer' noun) in the masculine plural. The al- means 'the'. The -ūna ending marks a plural group of males in the subject form, used for the subject or the thing being described. It names those who characteristically 'lie'.
14.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to speak falsehood

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
2.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: "And His mercy" — raḥma is mercy, compassion, and tender care; joined to a 'His'. Opened by the conjunction 'and'.
5.grammar: A feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'hu' ('his'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject or the thing being asserted. The noun's tāʾ marbūṭa is written as an open tāʾ (ت) because a pronoun is attached. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
7.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
7.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

8.meaning: And the Hereafter / the final, lasting life — the world to come after death, contrasted with the present worldly life.
8.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a feminine adjective used as a noun, 'the Last (abode/life)', i.e. the Hereafter. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or follows a preposition or oath particle.
8.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

9.meaning: An emphatic statement that a punishment or affliction 'would surely have touched/afflicted you' — the verb pictures harm coming into contact with a person, prefixed with an oath-like 'surely' that strongly affirms the outcome, and ending in 'you (plural).'
9.grammar: An emphatic 'la-' + a past-tense verb ('he/it') + the attached object 'you all.' This 'la-…' on a past verb is the answer to a hypothetical ('had it not been…, surely…'), affirming what would have happened.
9.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, come into contact

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
11.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

12.meaning: To pour forth and stream out together in a surging multitude; said of a crowd moving off in a flood, hence 'to depart en masse' or 'to press onward in throngs'.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb, Form IV. The suffix -tum means 'you (plural masculine) did' the action, so the whole word reads 'you (all) poured forth / streamed away'. Form IV (the initial a-) gives the sense of the subjects setting themselves moving in a flood.
12.root: ف-ي-ض (f-y-ḍ) — to overflow, pour forth, stream abundantly

13.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
13.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

14.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
14.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

15.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
15.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'You (all) receive/pass it along' — Form V of the root 'to meet': to take something up eagerly as it comes to you, catching it tongue from tongue; used of picking up and relaying talk.

parts.en: take up, receive (Form V stem of 'meet')

2.grammar: The ta- prefix with the -w...-na ending marks 'you (plural)' in the present tense; the -na is the indicative plural ending, used for a plain statement of what is actually happening. The doubled middle letter (Form V) adds eagerness/repetition to the base sense of 'meet'. The final -hu is the object pronoun 'it'.

3.meaning: 'With your tongues' — alsina is the plural of lisān, 'tongue', the organ of speech and by extension speech or language itself.
3.grammar: bi- is the preposition 'with/by means of'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, required after a preposition. The suffix -kum is the attached pronoun 'your (plural)', marking possession: 'the tongues OF YOU ALL'.

4.meaning: 'And you (all) say' — from qāla, the everyday verb of saying and speaking.

parts.en: plural indicative ending ('you all', plain statement)

4.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending together mean 'you (plural)' in the present tense; -ūna is the full indicative ending, the default form for stating what actually happens or is happening (when this ending loses its -na, the verb has entered a dependent or commanded mood).

5.meaning: 'With your mouths' — afwāh is the plural of fam, 'mouth'; speaking 'with the mouths' suggests words merely uttered, without grounding in knowledge or heart.
5.grammar: bi- is the preposition 'with/by means of'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, which a noun must take after a preposition. The suffix -kum is 'your (plural)', tying the mouths to their owners: 'the mouths OF YOU ALL'.

6.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
6.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

7.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
7.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'knowledge' — sure, established knowing; awareness of facts based on evidence, the opposite of ignorance or guesswork.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('some knowledge', not 'the knowledge'), and the nominative case typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed.

11.meaning: "And you consider/reckon it" — from ḥasiba, to suppose, deem, or count something as being a certain way; an act of mental estimation rather than certain knowledge, addressed to a group with an attached "it".
11.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a group: the ta- prefix plus the -ūna ending together mean "you (plural) do/are doing" — the full -ūna form marks the plain indicative mood (a straightforward statement). The attached -hu is an object pronoun, "it/him", so the whole word packs a sentence: "and you consider it (to be) ...".

12.meaning: "A light, trifling thing" — hayyin describes something easy, slight, of little weight or consequence; something treated as no big deal.
12.grammar: An adjective of the fayʿil (فَيْعِل) pattern used with hollow (weak-middle) roots — the same shape as sayyid and mayyit; the pattern's y fuses with the root's weak middle letter to give the doubled -yy- heard in hayyin. The -an ending (double fatḥa, written with alif) is the indefinite accusative: it commonly marks the object of a verb or the second part of statements like "you deem it X" — i.e. the state or description something is held to be.

13.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
13.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

14.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
14.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: Great, immense, mighty, or tremendous — describing something vast in scale, weight, or significance.
16.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('great, mighty'). The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative; an adjective in this form typically agrees with and describes an indefinite nominative noun.
16.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

3.meaning: 'You (all) heard it' — from samiʿa, to hear, perceive with the ear; the form bundles the hearers ('you all') and the thing heard ('it') into one word.

parts.en: you all (2nd masculine plural, with joining vowel -ū)

3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum means 'you (plural)' and marks the action as completed; it lengthens to -tumū simply to join smoothly onto the following pronoun. The final -hu is the object pronoun 'it' — so subject, tense, and object all sit in the endings.

4.meaning: 'You (plural) said' — to say, speak, or utter. The verb covers any act of stating or declaring something in words.
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -tum marks the masculine plural 'you (all)' as the doers of a completed action — it signals both the past tense and that the speakers being addressed are a group. (This is a hollow verb: its middle root letter is a wāw, which surfaces as a long ā in the base form qāla but reduces to a short u, giving qul-, before a consonant-initial suffix like -tum.)
4.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

5.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
5.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

6.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
6.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to us' or 'for us / belonging to us' — combining the preposition 'to/for' with the attached pronoun 'us', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward the speakers.
7.grammar: A preposition fused with an attached pronoun. The base 'li' ('to/for') shifts to 'la' before an attached pronoun, so it appears here with a fatḥa as 'la'; the suffix 'nā' means 'us' (first-person plural). Together it conveys 'for us' — indicating benefit, possession, or direction.

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: "That we speak / talk about" — Form V of the root of speech: takallama, to talk, utter, engage in speech, with "we" as the doer.

parts.en: speak / talk (Form V stem, with subjunctive -a)

9.grammar: The na- prefix means "we". The stem takallam- is Form V (ta- + doubled middle letter), a pattern of engaging oneself in an act — here, engaging in speech. The final -a is the subjunctive mood ending: it appears when the verb follows particles like an ("that") or li- ("in order to"), i.e. "(that) we should speak".

10.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'by this' or 'with this' — the preposition 'with/by means of' joined to the demonstrative 'this', pointing to something near or just mentioned.
10.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with', 'by') attached to the demonstrative pronoun hādhā ('this', masculine singular). The demonstrative is invariable in form here; the preposition indicates instrument or means ('by means of this') or association ('with this').

11.meaning: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
11.grammar: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
11.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

12.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
12.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

13.meaning: A stunning slander: buhtān is a lie or false accusation so brazen that it leaves its victim dumbfounded — from a verb meaning to confound or strike with astonishment. It denotes calumny of the gravest kind.
13.grammar: A noun on the intensive fuʿlān pattern, which conveys magnitude — not just a lie but an enormity of falsehood. The -un ending (double ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative: it marks the word as a subject or as the predicate of a statement ("this is a slander").
13.root: ب-ه-ت (b-h-t) — to stun, confound, accuse falsely

14.meaning: Great, immense, mighty, or tremendous — describing something vast in scale, weight, or significance.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('great, mighty'). The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative; an adjective in this form typically agrees with and describes an indefinite nominative noun.
14.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: "He admonishes you" — from waʿaẓa: to exhort, counsel, and warn in a way that softens the heart; loving admonition that reminds of consequences, with "you all" attached as its object.
1.grammar: The ya- prefix means "he". The root begins with wāw (w-ʿ-ẓ), which regularly drops out in the present tense — hence yaʿiẓu, not yawʿiẓu. The -u vowel on the stem is the indicative mood: a plain ongoing statement ("he admonishes"). The suffix -kum(u) is the object pronoun "you all"; its final u is a helping vowel for smooth pronunciation.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: You (plural) return, go back, revert, do something again. From a root meaning 'to return / repeat,' it denotes coming back to a prior state or resuming a previous course of action.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks a plural masculine 'you all.' The missing final nūn (-ū not -ūna) signals the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after conditional or purpose particles ('if you return …').
4.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, to repeat, to come back

5.meaning: "For the like of it" — mithl means a likeness, an equivalent, something of the same kind; with li- ("to/for") and "it" attached: anything resembling or comparable to it.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ("to/for") forces the genitive case, shown by the -i on mithl. The attached pronoun -hi ("it") is the -hu pronoun changed to -hi because it follows an i-sound. Mithl + pronoun forms a possessive chain: literally "the like OF it".

6.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
6.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
8.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

9.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

9.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
9.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: "And He makes clear" — Form II bayyana: to clarify, expound, make plain and distinct so that no ambiguity remains.
1.grammar: The yu- prefix means "he" (the u-vowel of the prefix is typical of Form II verbs). The doubled middle letter (bayyana) is the Form II causative pattern: to MAKE something clear, not merely to be clear. The final -u is the indicative mood ending, marking a plain statement of ongoing action.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
3.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

4.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
4.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

7.meaning: Wise; possessing perfect, far-reaching wisdom that places everything in its right order and purpose. It implies sound judgement and flawless governance, not merely cleverness.
7.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, expressing a settled, profound quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks a subject or a predicate describing something ("is wise").
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — wisdom, sound judgement, to govern

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: "They love / cherish / hold dear" — to feel deep affection or fondness for someone or something. Describes an ongoing or habitual loving by a group.
3.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb with the yu-…-ūna frame meaning "they" (a group of males). The -ūna ending marks the plain present tense for a plural "they" subject (not negated, commanded, or made conditional). The yu- prefix belongs to this verb's particular pattern of loving.
3.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: "(That) it should spread / circulate" — from shāʿa: for news or talk to go around, become public, be broadcast among people.
5.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a feminine singular subject ("it/she"). The verb has a weak middle letter (sh-y-ʿ), giving the long ī. The final -a is the subjunctive mood: this form appears after particles like an ("that") or expressions of wish/purpose — "(that) it should spread".
5.root: ش-ي-ع (sh-y-ʿ) — to spread, circulate, become public

6.meaning: "The gross indecency" — fāḥisha denotes an act of flagrant immorality, something shamelessly excessive that oversteps all bounds of decency; classically used above all of sexual sin and public obscenity.
6.grammar: Al- is the definite article "the". Fāḥisha is on the active-participle pattern fāʿila used as a noun: that which is itself excessive/outrageous. The final -u is the nominative case, marking the word as the subject of its clause — the one doing or undergoing the action being stated.
6.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — exceeding bounds, obscenity, gross excess

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
9.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

12.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
12.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
14.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
14.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

15.meaning: And the Hereafter / the final, lasting life — the world to come after death, contrasted with the present worldly life.
15.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a feminine adjective used as a noun, 'the Last (abode/life)', i.e. the Hereafter. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or follows a preposition or oath particle.
15.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

16.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
16.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
16.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

17.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

18.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and', or here 'while'), joined to the standalone pronoun 'antum' meaning 'you (all)'. It often introduces a circumstantial clause: 'while you …', 'and you …'.
18.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle that can mean 'and' or introduce a background clause ('while …'). 'antum' is the detached subject pronoun for a masculine plural addressee, 'you all'. As an independent pronoun it takes no case ending; the final '-um' is simply part of the word.

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: A verb addressed to a group: 'you (all) know', 'you have knowledge', 'you are aware'. From the root meaning 'to know'.
20.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject and is the full 'indicative' form, signalling an ongoing, factual statement ('you (all) do know'), as opposed to the shortened '-ū' used after certain particles.

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
2.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
2.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: "And His mercy" — raḥma is mercy, compassion, and tender care; joined to a 'His'. Opened by the conjunction 'and'.
5.grammar: A feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'hu' ('his'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject or the thing being asserted. The noun's tāʾ marbūṭa is written as an open tāʾ (ت) because a pronoun is attached. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

6.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
6.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
7.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

8.meaning: Most kind, gentle, and compassionate; one who is full of tender pity and gentleness. Raʾūf is an intensive form stressing deep, abundant kindness — a name/attribute of Allah meaning 'the Ever-Gentle, Most Compassionate.'

parts.en: full of kindness / most gentle (the final -un is the nominative ending with tanwīn, marking an indefinite predicate)

8.grammar: An intensive adjective ('one full of …') describing abundant kindness. The final '-un' is the nominative case ending together with tanwīn (the '-n' that marks an indefinite noun): it typically marks the word as a subject or, as here, a predicate/description ('… is most kind'). The intensive pattern stresses depth and constancy of the quality.

9.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: 'You (plural) follow' — a verb meaning to come after, pursue, take as a guide, or obey and imitate; addressed to a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form VIII), second-person masculine plural ('you follow'). The ta- prefix marks the addressee 'you'; the -ū ending marks a masculine plural 'you all'. The dropped final nūn (here -ū rather than -ūna) signals that the verb is in a subjunctive/jussive mood, typical after particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
5.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, come after, pursue

6.meaning: Footsteps, footprints, or paths — the steps and tracks left by walking; figuratively, the way or course someone treads.
6.grammar: A feminine sound plural ('footsteps, paths'; plural of khuṭwa). The -āt is the feminine plural marker; the final -i is the ending such plurals take in the genitive, which generally links the word to a following noun ('footsteps OF …') or follows a preposition.

7.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
7.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

8.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
8.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

9.meaning: "(Whoever) follows" — Form VIII ittabaʿa: to follow deliberately, walk in the footsteps of, take as a guide or model; a more engaged following than the simple verb.
9.grammar: The ya- prefix means "he". The doubled t is the mark of Form VIII (ittabaʿa), a pattern of taking an action upon oneself — following intentionally. The bare ending with NO final vowel (sukūn on the ʿayn) is the jussive mood: the clipped form used in conditional sentences ("whoever follows..."), after "lam" (did not), and in commands.

10.meaning: Footsteps, footprints, or paths — the steps and tracks left by walking; figuratively, the way or course someone treads.
10.grammar: A feminine sound plural ('footsteps, paths'; plural of khuṭwa). The -āt is the feminine plural marker; the final -i is the ending such plurals take in the genitive, which generally links the word to a following noun ('footsteps OF …') or follows a preposition.

11.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
11.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
11.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

12.meaning: A cluster of three elements: a connective 'so/then', the emphasis particle 'inna' that strongly affirms a statement ('indeed, truly'), and 'he/it'. Together: 'so indeed he / then truly it'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connecting particle showing sequence or consequence ('so, then'). 'inna' is an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the sentence that follows and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The attached 'hu' is that pronoun, 'he/it', here serving as the subject being emphasized.

13.meaning: 'He commands / orders / bids' — the act of giving orders or enjoining, said of a single doer, in the present tense.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final '-u' is the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or general/habitual action.

14.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'to/with immorality (al-faḥshāʾ)' — al-faḥshāʾ being gross indecency, shameful and outrageous conduct, especially sexual immorality and any flagrant moral excess.
14.grammar: A definite noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with, by, to'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required after a preposition and marks the noun as the object of that preposition.
14.root: ف-ح-ش (f-ḥ-sh) — to be excessive, grossly indecent

15.meaning: What is recognized as wrong, objectionable, and disowned; conduct that sound nature and revelation alike reject. Literally 'the disapproved/unrecognized', the opposite of what is right and accepted (maʿrūf).
15.grammar: A passive participle ('something disapproved/rejected') made definite with 'the' and joined by 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case, typically marking it as following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun.
15.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to not recognize, to deny, to find objectionable

16.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

16.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

17.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
17.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
17.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

18.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
18.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

19.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
19.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
19.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

20.meaning: "And His mercy" — raḥma is mercy, compassion, and tender care; joined to a 'His'. Opened by the conjunction 'and'.
20.grammar: A feminine noun with the attached possessive pronoun 'hu' ('his'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject or the thing being asserted. The noun's tāʾ marbūṭa is written as an open tāʾ (ت) because a pronoun is attached. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.

21.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
21.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

22.meaning: "(He would) have been pure / grown in purity" — zakā combines two ideas the root always carries together: purity and growth. To be zakī is to be cleansed of taint and to flourish because of it.
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular: "he was/became pure". The root's final letter is weak (w/y), so the verb ends in the long -ā typical of "defective" verbs like zakā and hadā — the -ā itself is the he-did past form, with no separate case ending. In conditional sentences the Arabic perfect often carries a "would have" sense.

23.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
23.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
23.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

24.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
24.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

25.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
25.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

26.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
26.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

27.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
27.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
28.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

29.meaning: A singular present verb: 'He purifies, He cleanses, He sanctifies.' It expresses making someone pure of sin and causing them to grow in goodness — a purification granted by Allah.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive (form II) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final long -ī is the indicative form of this 'weak-ending' verb, expressing an ongoing or habitual action ('He purifies').

30.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
30.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

31.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
31.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
31.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

32.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
32.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
32.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

33.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
33.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

34.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
34.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: "Let (him not) swear / fall short" — Form VIII from a root meaning both to swear an oath and to fall short; classically understood as swearing an oath to withhold something (especially to stop doing good to someone).

parts.en: swear (an oath) / fall short (Form VIII stem)

2.grammar: The ya- prefix means "he". The stem is Form VIII (iʾtalā) of a final-weak root; in the jussive mood the long final vowel is shortened — yaʾtalī becomes yaʾtali, ending in a short -i with the long ī (and its letter yāʾ) gone. That clipped ending is how final-weak verbs show the jussive, the mood used with the prohibitive lā ("let him not...") and in conditions and commands.
2.root: أ-ل-و (ʾ-l-w) — to fall short, withhold; (Form VIII) to swear an oath

3.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
3.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
3.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

4.meaning: Bounty, grace, abundant favour — generous giving beyond what is owed or merely sufficient; overflowing goodness and surplus.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the bounty'). The al- prefix means 'the'; the final -i is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or when the noun is possessed by a preceding word (the '… OF …' relationship).
4.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to exceed, be left over; abundance, surplus, favour

5.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
5.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
5.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

6.meaning: "And the ampleness (of means)" — saʿa is roominess, capacity, abundance: having space and plenty, especially ample wealth and resources.
6.grammar: Wa- is "and"; al- is "the" — and because s is a "sun letter", the l of the article assimilates and the s doubles in pronunciation (as-saʿa). The noun comes from a root whose first letter (wāw) has dropped from this form. The -i ending is the genitive case: the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ("... of ...").

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

8.meaning: "(That) they give" — Form IV ātā, literally "to make come (to someone)", i.e. to give, grant, bestow.
8.grammar: The yu- prefix (u-vowel typical of Form IV) plus the plural -ū means "they". Crucially, the ending is bare -ū, not the full -ūna: dropping the -na is the mark of the subjunctive/jussive moods, used after particles like an ("that") or in clauses of purpose and command — "(that) they give". The final silent alif is just a spelling convention after plural -ū.
8.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to give, bring to

9.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

10.meaning: Nearness, kinship, closeness of relation — the bond of being near in blood, hence 'relatives' or 'near kin'. The word names the quality of family closeness itself.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' (the). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role through context rather than a changing final vowel. The sense is abstract: 'nearness of kin'.
10.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, close; nearness, kinship

11.meaning: 'And the needy / the poor' — those in straitened circumstances, lacking what they need. Often denotes the destitute who are too restrained by poverty to provide for themselves. Joined by 'and'.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') plus the definite broken plural of miskīn ('needy person'), on the mafāʿīl pattern. The final -a is the accusative case. Because the word is definite (with al-), it takes the regular full case endings, so this -a is simply the accusative of a definite noun. (The diptote rule, by which such a plural shares one -a for both genitive and accusative, applies only when it is indefinite.)
11.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, being subdued; (miskīn) one stilled by poverty

12.meaning: And the emigrants — those who left their homes and migrated for the sake of faith, abandoning one place for another. The leading 'and' joins it to a preceding item; the rest is a plural active participle naming such migrants as a class.
12.grammar: 'And' (wa) + al- ('the') + a Form III active participle ('one who migrates'); Form III often carries a sense of mutual or directed action. The -īna ending is a masculine sound plural in the object or prepositional (accusative/genitive) case — the form used when such a word is an object or follows a preposition, as opposed to subject-case -ūna.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
14.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: "And let them pardon" — ʿafā means to pardon by effacing: to wipe an offense away as wind effaces footprints in sand, giving up any claim against the offender.
16.grammar: The l- is the "lām of command": prefixed to a present-tense verb it turns it into "let him/them do...". A verb after this lām takes the jussive mood — for a plural that means the ending is bare -ū with the -na dropped (yaʿfūna becomes yaʿfū). The root's final weak letter merges into that -ū. So the word reads: and + let + they + pardon.
16.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — pardon, effacing, letting go

17.meaning: "And let them overlook" — ṣafaḥa is to turn the broad side of one's face away from an offense: to disregard it graciously, without reproach; a step beyond pardon, forgetting as well as forgiving.
17.grammar: Same build as "walyaʿfū": wa- "and" + the lām of command ("let...") + ya- "they" + the verb in the jussive mood. The plural ending -ū without the usual -na is precisely the jussive form the command-lām requires: "let them overlook". The silent alif after -ū is purely orthographic.
17.root: ص-ف-ح (ṣ-f-ḥ) — turning the face aside, gracious overlooking

18.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
18.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

19.meaning: You (plural) love, are devoted to, or hold dear — an imperfect verb of affection addressed to a group. The underlying sense is loving, cherishing, and being drawn toward someone or something.
19.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb of Form IV (the standard verb 'to love', aḥabba / yuḥibbu, from a doubled root). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') in the indicative mood — the plain factual form for ongoing/future action. Dropping the final -na would signal subjunctive or jussive instead.
19.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, holding dear

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
20.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

21.meaning: He forgives / that He forgive: to pardon and cover over sins; the form points to a single doer's act of forgiving as a hoped-for or purposed outcome.

parts.en: he (masculine, present-tense prefix), doubled by assimilation

21.grammar: An imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he …'). The ya- prefix marks one masculine doer; here the yāʾ carries a shaddah (it is doubled) because a preceding consonant has assimilated into it (idghām) — the l of the purpose particle li- ('so that') merges into the following yāʾ, so 'li-yaghfira' is pronounced 'liyyaghfira'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, taken after particles like 'so that / in order that', giving the sense of a purposed or anticipated act ('that He may forgive').
21.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, cover over, pardon

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

23.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
