50.grammar: A noun of exception/negation meaning 'something other than'. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. So it sets up the sense 'other than [the following thing]'.

51.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
51.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

52.meaning: The desire/need — irba means want or need, and in usage particularly sexual desire for women; 'those without irba' are men lacking such inclination.
52.grammar: A definite noun (al- 'the') with the genitive -i ending, which generally marks a noun that follows a preposition or completes an 'of' phrase (e.g. 'possessors of desire'). The tāʾ marbūṭa (-at) shows the noun is grammatically feminine.

53.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
53.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

54.meaning: A noun meaning 'the men / the menfolk' — adult human males. By extension the root conveys manliness and the standing on one's feet, but the plain sense of this plural is 'men.'
54.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun ('the men'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…' (as in 'of the men / among the men'). The 'r' is doubled in pronunciation because the 'l' of 'al-' (the) assimilates into it.
54.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manliness, going on foot

55.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two or more options, linking possibilities of which one applies.
55.grammar: A connecting particle meaning 'or'. Its base form is aw; the added -i is a 'helping' vowel given to the otherwise-silent final consonant to smooth the link to a following word that begins with a connecting (hamzat-waṣl) alif. It is not a case ending — particles do not take cases.

56.meaning: The children — ṭifl means a young child or infant; in Arabic the singular can be used collectively for children as a class. The root evokes tenderness and softness of infancy.

parts.en: child, infant (can stand for children as a class)

56.grammar: A definite noun with the genitive -i ending — the case generally used after a preposition or in an 'of' chain. The al- assimilates in pronunciation to the ṭ (aṭ-ṭifl), which is why the t doubles in speech though it is written al-.

57.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
57.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

58.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

58.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

59.meaning: '(That) they prevail / gain the upper hand / become dominant' — a present/future verb whose root sense is to appear or come out on top; in this form it means to overcome, gain mastery over, or become dominant over an opponent. It refers to a group of males.
59.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a masculine subject; the plural ending here is -ū (a group of males), and the dropped final -na (compared with the full -ūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after particles of purpose, negation, or condition, rather than a plain factual statement.
59.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become manifest, prevail

60.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
60.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

61.meaning: Private aspects/nakedness — ʿawrāt is the plural of ʿawra: anything private, vulnerable, or shameful to expose, especially the intimate parts of the body.

parts.en: private parts, vulnerable/intimate matters (plural of ʿawra)

61.grammar: A sound feminine plural (-āt). On such plurals the -i ending does double duty: it is the regular genitive ('… of …', or after a preposition) and also the form this plural takes when it is a direct object, since -āt plurals never take the -a object ending.
61.root: ع-و-ر (ʿ-w-r) — exposure, vulnerability, a gap or weakness

62.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
62.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

63.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
63.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

64.meaning: They (women) strike/stamp — the basic verb ḍaraba, 'to strike', which with feet means to stamp or beat them on the ground.
64.grammar: An imperfect (present-future) verb. The ya- prefix marks third person, and the -na ending marks a feminine plural subject: 'they (women) strike'. Verbs with this feminine -na are invariable — the ending stays the same regardless of mood, so the same written form serves for statements and for 'let them not…' commands.

65.meaning: With their feet — arjul is the plural of rijl ('foot, leg').

parts.en: their (belonging to a group of women)

65.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') puts the following noun into the genitive, shown by the -i ending — the standard rule after every preposition. The -hinna suffix is the feminine plural 'their'.
65.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, leg (also the root of rajul, 'man')

66.meaning: So that it may be made known — a purpose expression built on the passive of 'to know': in order that something becomes known (without naming who comes to know it).
66.grammar: The li- here is the 'lām of purpose' ('in order that'), and after it the verb takes the subjunctive -a ending — the mood Arabic uses for intended or aimed-at actions. The vowel pattern yu-...-a (yuʿlama, not yaʿlamu) is the passive voice: 'be known' rather than 'know', leaving the knower unstated.

67.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
67.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

68.meaning: They (women) conceal/keep hidden — Form IV of the root of hiddenness: to actively keep something out of sight.
68.grammar: An imperfect verb in Form IV (the causative pattern, akhfā: 'to make hidden' = to conceal). The yu- prefix marks third person in this verb pattern, and the -na ending marks the feminine plural subject — a group of women doing the concealing. With the feminine -na the form is invariable across moods.

69.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
69.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

70.meaning: Their adornment — zīna: jewellery, ornaments, finery, and by extension beauty that is adorned; here in its genitive shape.

parts.en: their (belonging to a group of women)

70.grammar: The -i ending is genitive: it generally marks the noun as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship with what precedes it (e.g. 'part of their adornment'). The -hinna suffix is 'their' for a group of women, pronounced hinna because it follows the i-vowel.

71.meaning: A plural command to 'turn back' — to repent, returning to Allah after sin. The verb tāba pictures repentance as physically turning around and coming back.
71.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a group: the -ū ending means 'you all', so the form orders a whole community, not one person, to repent. The wa- prefix simply joins it to what precedes ('and…').

72.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
72.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

73.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
73.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

74.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
74.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

75.meaning: A vocative marker meaning 'O…!' — a particle of direct address used to call out to or summon the one being spoken to, the way 'O' or 'hey, you' opens a direct appeal.
75.grammar: A vocative construction used to address someone directly. It is not a verb and has no tense; it functions purely to flag that a call or appeal to the listener follows. It is normally paired with a following noun naming whoever is being summoned.

76.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
76.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

77.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

77.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

78.meaning: You attain success / prosper / flourish. To achieve true success and lasting well-being — winning what is sought and being saved from loss.
78.grammar: A present-tense verb for the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The tu- prefix (from the fourth verb pattern) signals a 'you' subject, and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood, stating it as an ongoing or factual reality.
78.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to succeed, prosper, thrive (originally to till/cultivate)

1.meaning: A plural command meaning 'give in marriage / arrange the marriage of' — the causative form: not 'marry someone yourself' but 'see that others get married'.
1.grammar: Form IV (causative) imperative: the a- of ankiḥ- turns 'marry' into 'cause to marry, marry off'. The -ū ending marks a plural command — 'you all' are told to do it. Wa- means 'and'.

2.meaning: 'The spouseless ones' — those currently without a marriage partner, whether never married, widowed, or divorced, of either sex. Plural of ayyim.
2.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- ('the') makes it refer to the whole class of unmarried people. Because the word ends in the long -ā sound (alif maqṣūrah), it cannot show a case vowel — its role in a sentence is understood, not written.

3.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
3.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

4.meaning: 'And the righteous / upright ones' — those who are morally sound, who do good and set things right in their conduct and dealings.
4.grammar: A definite plural active participle used for people ('the … ones'), joined by 'and' (wa-) with 'the' (al-). The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the object/oblique case (for direct objects and after prepositions).
4.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — being sound, good, upright; setting right

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'Your male slaves/servants' — ʿibād is a plural of ʿabd, 'slave, servant'; the same word family gives ʿibādah, worshipful service, since every creature is ultimately a servant of Allah.
6.grammar: The -i before -kum is the genitive case vowel: it appears when the word follows a preposition or is linked in an 'of'-relationship. The suffix -kum means 'your', addressing a group of people.

7.meaning: 'And your female slaves' — imāʾ is the plural of amah, a bondwoman or female servant.
7.grammar: Wa- means 'and', joining this noun to a previous one. The -i on imāʾi is the genitive case vowel, matching the noun it is paired with; -kum is the attached pronoun 'your' (said to a group).

8.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
8.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

9.meaning: To be, to become, or to come to be — the basic verb of being and existence, also used as a helper to place a statement in past or continuing time.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of being, third person masculine plural ('they'). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-party subject and the long '-ū' marks the masculine plural 'they'. The stem is bare 'kūn' with no indicative '-u' vowel, and the missing final 'n' on the ending shows subjunctive/jussive mood — typically governed by a preceding particle ('that they be…' / 'they would be').
9.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

10.meaning: 'Poor ones' — plural of faqīr, a person in need, one whose back is (figuratively) broken by want; in the Qur'anic worldview all creatures are fuqarāʾ, needy, before Allah the Self-Sufficient.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural on the pattern fuʿalāʾ. Words of this pattern are 'diptotes': they never take tanwīn (the -n sound), and a single -a vowel serves them even where other nouns would show a different ending. The final -a here is that diptote case ending.

11.meaning: 'He will enrich them / free them of need' — the causative of ghinā (self-sufficiency, wealth): to make someone no longer needy.
11.grammar: Form IV (causative) verb: yu- marks 'he' as the doer. The final long -ī of the stem is dropped (yughni, not yughnī) — that shortening is the jussive mood, the form a verb takes as the result-clause of a condition ('if…, then he will…') or after certain particles. The -u after -him is just a helping vowel for smooth pronunciation.
11.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — wealth, being free of need

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
14.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
14.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

15.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
15.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

16.meaning: An adjective meaning 'vast, ample, all-embracing, boundless' — wide in capacity, encompassing; of Allah it conveys limitless reach in knowledge, mercy, and bounty.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who is vast/encompassing') used adjectivally. The ending '-un' is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn), marking it as 'a vast one' and as a subject or predicate.
16.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — breadth, capacity, amplitude, to encompass

17.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: 'And let him seek chastity / restrain himself' — a third-person command built on Form X of ʿaffa: to actively strive for ʿiffah, self-restraint from what is unlawful, especially sexual continence.
1.grammar: The lām of command (l-) before a verb creates a third-person order: 'let him…'. That lām puts the verb in the jussive mood (no final vowel of its own); the little -i heard at the end is only a helping vowel added so the word can join smoothly to a following word beginning with a consonant cluster. The sta- infix marks Form X, 'to seek/strive for' the root idea.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
4.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
4.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

5.meaning: 'Marriage' — the verbal noun nikāḥ, the marriage contract and union itself; by extension, the means to marry.
5.grammar: The -an ending is tanwīn in the accusative case: it marks the word as indefinite ('a marriage', not 'the marriage') and typically as the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon or attained.

6.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
6.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

7.meaning: 'He enriches them / frees them of need' — the same causative verb aghnā: to make someone self-sufficient, no longer dependent.
7.grammar: Form IV (causative), 'he' marked by yu-. The -a vowel on the stem's final consonant (yughniya, not yughnī) is the subjunctive mood, which appears after particles meaning 'so that', 'until', or 'that' — it frames the enriching as a goal or awaited outcome. The final -u of -humu is a helping vowel.
7.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — wealth, being free of need

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
10.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
10.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

11.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

12.meaning: 'they seek / pursue / strive after' — a group actively looking for and aiming to obtain something, whether a material gain or a spiritual reward. It conveys ongoing endeavour and quest.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb of the reflexive Form VIII. The 'ya-' prefix plus the -ūna ending together mean 'they (masculine) seek'. The retained 'na' marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they do seek'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by certain particles.
12.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive for

13.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
13.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

14.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
14.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

15.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
15.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

16.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
16.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
16.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

17.meaning: 'Then make a written contract with them' — the technical verb for mukātabah, the emancipation deed by which a slave buys freedom in installments; Form III implies a mutual, two-party writing.
17.grammar: Fa- means 'then/so', marking a consequence. Kātibū is a Form III imperative — the long ā after the first root letter signals doing something *with* another party — and the -ū ending makes it a command to a group. The suffix -hum ('them') is the object of the command.

18.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
18.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

19.meaning: 'You (all) have known / you knew' — a past-tense verb stating that a group came to know, recognized, or were aware of something.
19.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-tum' is the attached subject pronoun for second-person masculine plural ('you all did it'). In the past tense the doer is shown by such endings rather than by a prefix.
19.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

20.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
20.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
20.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

21.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
21.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.

22.meaning: 'And give them' — from ātā, the Qur'an's elevated verb of giving and granting, often used of bestowing wealth, scripture, or favor.
22.grammar: A plural imperative: the -ū ending commands a group ('you all give'). The attached pronoun -hum ('them') names who receives. Wa- is simply 'and'. The verb is Form IV of the root, which turns 'to come' into 'to bring/hand over, to give'.

23.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
23.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

24.meaning: 'Wealth / property (of…)' — māl covers money, livestock, and possessions generally; whatever a person owns.
24.grammar: The -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun in an 'of'-relationship ('the wealth OF…') or shows that it follows a preposition. Having no tanwīn, the word stands in a construct chain, leaning on the noun after it.

25.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
25.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

26.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
26.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

27.meaning: 'He has given / granted you' — a verb of bestowing, with 'He' as the giver and 'you (plural)' as the recipients; to hand over and grant something so that the receivers come to have it.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The third-person masculine singular subject 'he' is carried within the bare verb form (ending in the long -ā). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you (a group)' — the ones given to.
27.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

28.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
28.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

29.meaning: 'You compel / force' — Form IV of a root meaning dislike and aversion: to push someone into what they hate against their will.
29.grammar: The tu- prefix means 'you' and the -ū ending makes it plural, 'you all'. In its full form this verb would end in -na (tukrihūna); the dropped -na is the shortened mood used after 'do not…' prohibitions or 'that you…' clauses — the form itself signals it sits under such a particle.
29.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — aversion, compulsion against one's will

30.meaning: 'Your young women / slave girls' — fatayāt is the plural of fatāh, literally 'young woman'; used as the gentler Qur'anic term for female servants.
30.grammar: A sound feminine plural (-āt). For such plurals the -i vowel does double duty: it is the ending used both for the genitive ('of…', after prepositions) and for the direct object. The suffix -kum means 'your', addressed to a group.

31.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
31.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
31.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

32.meaning: 'Prostitution' — bighāʾ, from a root meaning to seek or overstep bounds: unlawful sexual commerce, wrongdoing pursued as a trade.
32.grammar: Definite noun: al- means 'the', naming the practice as a known class of act. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or in an 'of'-phrase.

33.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
33.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

34.meaning: 'They (women) desired / willed' — the past tense of arāda, 'to want, intend', with a specifically feminine plural subject.
34.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, Form IV. The -na ending is the feminine plural subject marker: it means the doers are 'they' and specifically women. Compare aradū, which would mean men (or a mixed group) wanted.

35.meaning: 'Guarding one's chastity' — taḥaṣṣun, from ḥiṣn, a fortress: to fortify oneself morally, keeping oneself walled off from unlawful intimacy.
35.grammar: A Form V verbal noun (pattern tafaʿʿul), meaning doing the action to or for oneself. The -an ending is indefinite accusative tanwīn, the case used for objects and for phrases stating purpose or state ('desiring chastity', 'as chastity').

36.meaning: A verb meaning 'so that you (plural) may seek / pursue / strive after'. It denotes seeking out, desiring, and exerting effort to obtain something — such as seeking bounty or favor.
36.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that / in order to') marks purpose and puts the present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the final -na is dropped, leaving -ū for 'you (masculine plural)'. The form VIII pattern (with the infixed -t-) gives the sense of actively seeking for oneself.

37.meaning: Something fleeting and incidental — a passing gain, a transient benefit or worldly advantage that quickly comes and goes, with no lasting permanence.
37.grammar: A noun with the '-a' accusative ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing sought or pursued) or otherwise the receiver of the action.
37.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to present/occur; that which is incidental or transient

38.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
38.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

39.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
39.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
39.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

40.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
40.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

41.meaning: 'He compels them (women)' — forces them, against their aversion, into something they hate.
41.grammar: Form IV verb with yu- marking 'he'. The stem carries no final vowel of its own (yukrih-, not yukrihu-): that bare ending is the jussive mood, the form verbs take inside 'whoever…' conditional phrasing. The suffix -hunna is the feminine plural object pronoun, 'them (women)'.
41.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — aversion, compulsion against one's will

42.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
42.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

43.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
43.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

44.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
44.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

45.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
45.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
45.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

46.meaning: 'Their (women's) being compelled' — ikrāh, the noun 'compulsion, coercion': the state of being forced. With the pronoun it names the coercion done to those women.
46.grammar: A Form IV verbal noun. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case vowel, the form used after a preposition or in an 'of'-chain ('after the compulsion of them'). The suffix -hinna is the feminine plural 'their', referring to women.
46.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — aversion, compulsion against one's will

47.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
47.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

48.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
48.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We sent down / We caused to descend — a past-tense verb (form IV of n-z-l) conveying the act of sending something down from a higher source, especially revelation, with 'We' as the doer.
2.grammar: Past tense. The '-nā' suffix is the subject pronoun 'we', so the whole word means 'we sent down'. The form IV pattern (a- prefix on the stem) gives a causative sense: to make something come down.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

3.meaning: 'To you (all)' — the preposition ilā, marking direction or destination ('toward, unto'), aimed at a plural 'you'.

parts.en: stray fragment — the first letter of the next word, carried over by the text extraction; not part of this word

3.grammar: The preposition ilā changes its final -ā to -ay whenever a pronoun is attached, giving ilay-kum. Prepositions take no case ending themselves; the attached -kum is the plural 'you' that the motion or address is directed toward. The detached hamza fragment after the word belongs to the following word, not to ilaykum, and carries no grammatical role here.

4.meaning: Signs / verses / evidentiary marks — the plural of 'āyah', a sign or token that points to something beyond itself; used for miraculous signs, natural wonders, and the discrete verses of revelation.
4.grammar: A sound feminine plural. The '-in' (nunation) ending marks it as indefinite ('signs', not 'the signs') and is the genitive/accusative (oblique) case form, typical of an object or a word governed by a preposition.
4.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that indicates something

5.meaning: 'Clarifying / making (things) clear' — a plural active participle from bayyana, 'to make plain': things that themselves shed clarity, that expound and distinguish truth.
5.grammar: The mu- prefix builds an active participle: 'that which makes clear'. The -āt marks a feminine plural (agreeing with a feminine or non-human plural noun it describes). The final -in is indefinite tanwīn in the case feminine plurals use for both genitive and object positions.

6.meaning: And an example, and a lesson — wamathalan is wa- (and) plus mathal (example, parable, likeness, lesson) in the indefinite accusative.

parts.en: noun, indefinite accusative: example, parable, lesson, likeness

6.grammar: Wa- coordinates with salafan. Mathalan is the indefinite accusative (-an tanwīn). Together with salafan it forms a second/third object of jaʿalnāhum: 'We made them a precedent and a lesson'.
6.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; example, parable, likeness, proverb

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: They were alone, withdrew in private, or were by themselves apart from others; to be in seclusion or privacy with someone.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb from a weak root, so the plural ending appears as -aw (written with a silent final alif). It means 'they' for a group of males and marks a completed action: 'they were alone / withdrew in private.'
9.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, alone, secluded; privacy

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
11.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

12.meaning: 'And an admonition' — earnest counsel or exhortation that warns and softens the heart, urging right conduct and cautioning against wrong. Mawʿiẓa is moral advice that both warns and moves.
12.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') plus a feminine noun. The ending 'tan' (tā' marbūṭa with tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an admonition') and accusative — the case used for an object or for something set up alongside a preceding accusative item.

13.meaning: 'For the mindful/God-conscious ones' — for those who have taqwa: a reverent, protective awareness of Allah that makes a person guard against wrongdoing and shield themselves from His displeasure. The word names people characterized by this watchful piety.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

13.grammar: A preposition li- ('for') joined to a definite masculine sound plural active participle. The -ina ending is the plural form used after a preposition or as an object (the oblique/genitive-accusative case) — 'for the … ones'. The participle pattern (muftaʿil) describes those who actively do the action: those who keep themselves guarded.

1.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
1.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

2.meaning: 'Light' — nūr, illumination in every sense: physical light, and by extension guidance, revelation, and the radiance by which things are truly seen.
2.grammar: The -u ending is the nominative case, the form of a sentence's subject or of the thing being talked about ('X is…'). Its lack of tanwīn shows it leans on a following noun in an 'of'-construction: 'the light OF…'.

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example; a similitude used to make something abstract vivid and understandable.
5.grammar: A singular noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described. Being without tanwīn here, it commonly stands as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the likeness OF …').
5.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, example

6.meaning: His light — the light belonging to Him (Allah). In Quranic usage, 'the light of Allah' refers to divine guidance, revelation, or the illumination that comes from Allah's truth.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun (nūr, 'light') in the genitive case, marked by -i, with the third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun -hi ('his') suffixed. The genitive is required because the noun is in a possessive construction (iḍāfa): the light 'of him / his light'. The -i before -hi is the genitive ending on the noun.

7.meaning: 'Like a niche' — mishkāt is a recess set into a wall to hold a lamp, so that the enclosure concentrates and reflects its glow; the word is prefixed with 'like', making a simile.
7.grammar: Ka- is the particle of comparison, 'like'. Any noun after ka- stands in the genitive case, and the -in ending is that genitive with tanwīn, marking the noun as indefinite: 'like a (certain) niche'. The tāʾ marbūṭah (-t-) is the feminine noun ending, pronounced -t- when a case vowel follows.
7.root: — (mishkāt is generally held to be a borrowed word for a lamp-niche, with no productive Arabic root)

8.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

9.meaning: A lamp — an instrument that holds a burning wick and gives off light. The pattern mifʿāl marks a tool or instrument, so the word literally means 'a thing by which light/morning-brightness is produced'.
9.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative and indefinite: nominative typically marks the subject or the predicate of a sentence ('X is a lamp'), and the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) signals 'a lamp' rather than 'the lamp'. The mi- at the start is part of the instrument pattern mifʿāl, 'tool for doing X'.

10.meaning: The lamp — the same instrument-noun for a light-giving lamp, now made definite with 'the', pointing back to a lamp already introduced or known.
10.grammar: Definite noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. The single -u ending is nominative, the case of a sentence's subject or topic — 'the lamp is/does ...'. Because the word is definite with al-, it takes plain -u, not the doubled -un of indefinite nouns.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: A glass — a vessel or object made of glass; the feminine ending -a marks a single glass thing (one glass vessel) as opposed to glass as a material (zujāj).
12.grammar: Feminine singular noun. The -in ending is genitive and indefinite: the genitive case typically follows a preposition ('in a glass') or links the word to a preceding noun ('... of a glass'); the tanwīn (doubled 'n') marks it as indefinite, 'a glass'. The tāʾ (t) of the feminine ending is pronounced because a case vowel follows.

13.meaning: The glass — the definite form of the same word: the specific glass vessel already in view.

parts.en: the (the l assimilates to the z: az-zujāja)

13.grammar: Definite feminine noun. Al- means 'the'; before the 'sun letter' z its l is not pronounced, giving az-zujāja. The final -u is nominative, the case of the subject or topic of a statement — 'the glass is ...'. Definite nouns take plain -u without tanwīn.

14.meaning: as if it / as though it were. Kaʾannahā is a comparative particle — 'as if it were', introducing an analogy or simile describing the serpent's movement.
14.grammar: Kaʾanna is a compound particle ('as if, as though'), with the attached feminine pronoun -hā ('it'). It introduces a comparative clause in the accusative.

15.meaning: A star, or bright celestial body (also used of planets) — a brilliant point of light in the sky.
15.grammar: Masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn: nominative marks the subject or the predicate of a nominal sentence ('it is a star'), and the tanwīn makes it indefinite — 'a star', some star, not a specific named one.

16.meaning: Brilliant, dazzlingly radiant — an adjective most commonly understood as formed from durr 'pearl': shining with the pure white luster of a pearl. Classical scholars also recorded a second derivation, from daraʾa 'to push, dart forth', picturing a star that shoots or streams with light; the 'pearl-like' reading is the more widespread.
16.grammar: An adjective (nisba type: noun + -iyy makes 'belonging to / like that noun', as in 'pearl' → 'pearly'). The -un ending is nominative indefinite; adjectives copy the case of the noun they describe, so this form accompanies a nominative indefinite noun.
16.root: د-ر-ر (d-r-r) — pearl; to flow/stream abundantly. (Derivation debated: some classical authorities instead traced the word to د-ر-ء (d-r-ʾ), 'to push, dart', with variant readings to match.)

17.meaning: It is kindled, it is lit — a passive verb: fire or light is set burning in it by another; from the verb awqada, 'to kindle a fire'.

parts.en: 'it ...' (3rd person prefix; in this verb form the prefix is yu- in both active and passive)
kindled (passive stem: the internal a-vowel, -qad- not -qid-, is what marks the passive)

17.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV ('to kindle'). In Form IV the prefix is yu- in both voices, so the passive is signalled by the vowel inside the stem: yūqadu ('it IS kindled') versus active yūqidu ('it kindles'). The final -u is the indicative mood, the normal ending of a plain present-tense statement of fact.
17.root: و-ق-د (w-q-d) — to kindle, light a fire

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: A tree — a single tree; the base sense of the root covers trees, bushes, and by extension things that branch and intertwine.
19.grammar: Feminine singular noun; the -a(t) ending marks one individual tree (shajar without it is trees collectively). The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn: genitive typically follows a preposition ('from a tree') or a preceding noun ('... of a tree'), and the tanwīn marks it as indefinite.
19.root: ش-ج-ر (sh-j-r) — tree; to branch, intertwine

20.meaning: Blessed — endowed with baraka: divine blessing, abundant lasting goodness that grows and remains; a passive participle, 'one that has been made blessed'.
20.grammar: A passive participle (Form III), used as an adjective. The mu- prefix builds participles: 'one that is/has been X-ed'. The feminine -a(t) shows it describes a feminine noun. The -in ending is genitive indefinite; adjectives match their noun's case, so this form goes with a genitive indefinite noun.

21.meaning: An olive tree (or a single olive) — the -a ending on zaytūn 'olives' singles out one olive tree; the same root gives zayt, 'olive oil'.
21.grammar: Feminine singular noun of unity: zaytūn is the collective 'olives/olive stock', and the -a(t) picks out one individual. The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn — the case used after prepositions or in '... of ...' chains, and as the case of an appositive or adjective following another genitive noun; indefinite ('an olive').

22.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
22.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

23.meaning: Eastern — belonging to the east, the direction of the sunrise; an adjective built from sharq 'east, place of sunrise'.
23.grammar: A feminine relative adjective: the -iyy suffix turns a noun into 'of/belonging to that thing' (east → eastern), and -a(t) makes it agree with a feminine noun. The -in ending is genitive indefinite; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes.
23.root: ش-ر-ق (sh-r-q) — sunrise, east, to shine forth

24.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
24.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

25.meaning: Western — belonging to the west, the direction of the sunset; an adjective built from gharb 'west, place of the sun's setting'.
25.grammar: A feminine relative adjective, exactly parallel to sharqiyya: noun gharb + -iyy ('of the west') + feminine -a(t). The -in ending is genitive indefinite, matching the case of the noun the adjective describes.
25.root: غ-ر-ب (gh-r-b) — setting of the sun, west; to depart

26.meaning: A present-tense verb 'it/he is almost (about to)'. It is a special 'verb of approach' meaning an action is on the verge of happening — nearly, but not quite, occurring.

parts.en: to be on the verge of (verb stem)

26.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he/it'; the stem is -kād-; the final -u is the separate indicative-mood ending. It normally governs a following present-tense verb, together meaning 'it almost (does) …'.
26.root: ك-و-د (k-w-d) — to be on the point of, almost do

27.meaning: Its oil / her oil — zayt is oil, especially olive oil, and the attached pronoun -hā ('its', referring to a feminine noun) marks possession.
27.grammar: Noun + possessive pronoun. The -u ending is nominative, the case of a subject or topic: 'its oil is/does ...'. The suffix -hā is the 3rd person feminine singular possessor, 'her/its'; a noun with an attached pronoun counts as definite, so it takes plain -u with no tanwīn.

28.meaning: It gives light, shines, glows — a causative verb: it radiates or produces illumination; from ḍawʾ, 'light, glow'.

parts.en: 'he/it ...' (3rd person prefix of a causative verb)

28.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (causative: 'to make light, give off light'). The yu- prefix means 'he/it' in this verb form. The final -u is the indicative mood — the ending of a straightforward present statement, 'it shines / would shine'.

29.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
29.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

30.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

30.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

31.meaning: (That it) touch it — from massa, 'to touch, come into contact with'; the attached -hu means 'it/him', so the whole form is 'touch(es) it'.

parts.en: touch (stem, with the doubled s spelled out)

31.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person feminine singular ('it', of a feminine noun), with the object pronoun -hu 'it/him' attached. The stem ends in a vowelless consonant (tamsas-, not tamassu-): that shortened, 'clipped' shape is the jussive mood, the form used after negating or conditional words like lam or law ('did not / even if ... touch'). In this doubled root (s-s) the jussive splits the doubled letter into two.

32.meaning: Fire — flame, blaze, or burning. The basic word for fire, and by extension a name for the Fire of punishment.
32.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a fire') and nominative — the case for a subject or a predicate.
32.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, illumination; fire as a source of light and heat

33.meaning: Light — nūr, illumination that makes things visible; used both of physical light and, very often, of spiritual light: guidance, revelation, and clarity from Allah.
33.grammar: Masculine singular noun. The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn: nominative is the case of the subject or of the predicate in an 'X is Y' sentence, and the tanwīn leaves it indefinite — 'light' in general, or '(a) light'.

34.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
34.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

35.meaning: A light — nūrin is a noun meaning light, radiance, or guidance, in the indefinite genitive after a preposition.
35.grammar: Nūr is a Form I noun from root n-w-r, in the indefinite genitive (tanwīn kasra -in). In context it refers to the light that Allah places in the heart of one He guides, or to the spiritual illumination that comes with guidance — 'Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord…?'
35.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to shine, to illuminate; light, radiance

36.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
36.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

37.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
37.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

38.meaning: To his light / for his light — the noun nūr 'light' with the preposition li- ('to, for, toward') in front and the possessive pronoun 'his/its' attached; who the possessor is depends on the surrounding sentence.
38.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, required on any noun after a preposition like li-. The suffix -hi is 'his/its' (3rd person masculine singular); it is normally -hu but shifts to -hi after an i-vowel. A noun with an attached pronoun is definite, so there is no tanwīn.

39.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
39.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

40.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
40.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
40.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

41.meaning: And He sets forth / strikes — literally 'to hit', commonly used for putting forward or coining a likeness or example; ongoing or repeated action.
41.grammar: Present/ongoing-tense verb: the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the final -u is the indicative ending typical of a plain present-tense statement. The leading wa- means 'and'. So: 'and he sets forth'.
41.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike, hit; to set forth, coin (a likeness)

42.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
42.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

43.meaning: The likenesses / parables / examples — the plural of mathal, a comparison, similitude, or illustrative example used to make a truth vivid. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the examples').
43.grammar: A definite plural noun (with al-). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

44.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
44.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

45.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
45.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
45.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

46.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
46.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

47.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
47.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
47.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

48.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
48.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
1.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

2.meaning: Houses — the plural of bayt, 'house, dwelling'; the word can cover ordinary homes as well as houses set apart for worship.
2.grammar: A broken (internal-change) plural: bayt → buyūt, like English 'mouse → mice'. The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn — the case a noun takes after a preposition ('in houses') or when linked to a preceding noun ('... of houses'); the tanwīn marks it indefinite.
2.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, dwelling; to spend the night

3.meaning: 'He gave permission / allowed / sanctioned' — from adhina, to permit and authorize; the same root carries the sense of giving ear and heeding.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject: 'he did (it).' It denotes an action viewed as finished.
3.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow, authorize; to give ear, listen, heed

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: (That) they be raised / exalted — a passive verb from rafaʿa, 'to raise, lift up, elevate in honor'; the passive means someone raises or exalts them.

parts.en: 'they/it (is) ...' (3rd feminine prefix; the u-vowel signals passive)

6.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular (the form Arabic uses for plurals of things). In this basic verb form (Form I) the u-vowel on the prefix together with the internal a-vowel (turfaʿa, not tarfaʿu) marks the passive: 'be raised' rather than 'raise'. The final -a is the subjunctive mood, the ending a verb takes after particles like an ('that ...'): 'that they be raised'.

7.meaning: And (that) it be mentioned / remembered — from dhakara, 'to mention, remember, invoke'; the passive means the naming or remembrance is done by others: 'be commemorated, be invoked'.

parts.en: 'it (is) ...' (3rd person prefix; the u-vowel signals passive)

7.grammar: The connector wa- 'and' + a present-tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular. In this basic verb form (Form I) the u-vowel on the prefix with internal a (yudhkara, not yadhkuru) is the passive shape: 'be mentioned'. The final -a is the subjunctive mood, used when the verb continues a 'that ...' clause — 'and that ... be mentioned'.

8.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

9.meaning: The noun 'name' joined to the pronoun 'his', meaning 'his name'; the carrying 'u-' is a connecting (helping) vowel sounded only when nothing precedes it.
9.grammar: A masculine noun ('name') with the -u (nominative) ending, the case typical of a subject. The attached '-hu' is a possessive pronoun ('his/its'). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, pronounced only at the start of an utterance.
9.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — name, elevation, that by which a thing is known

10.meaning: 'He / it glorifies, declares free of all imperfection' — a present-tense verb proclaiming Allah's absolute transcendence above every flaw.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it'). The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain, ongoing statement of fact. The verb means to extol Allah as utterly beyond any imperfection or likeness.
10.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; to declare Allah free of all imperfection

11.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

12.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
12.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

13.meaning: 'In / at the morning(s).' Al-ghuduww denotes the early part of the day, the time of forenoon or morning — the period of setting out at daybreak. The prefixed bi- adds 'in', 'at', or 'during'.
13.grammar: A masculine noun made definite by al- ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('in / at'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which is the case a noun takes after a preposition such as bi-.
