20.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, approving

21.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
21.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

22.meaning: 'And He will most surely exchange for them' — to swap one thing for another, replace a condition with its opposite. The doubled form suggests a thorough change-over.
22.grammar: Form II verb (baddala, 'to exchange, replace') with the full oath-emphasis frame: la- plus the doubled -anna ending = 'He absolutely will…'. yu- marks 'He'; the attached -hum ('them') names those for whose benefit the exchange is made. This verb typically takes two objects: the people, then the thing swapped.

23.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
23.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

24.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
24.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
24.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

25.meaning: Their fear — khawf is fear or dread, especially anxious apprehension of danger; owned by 'them' through the attached pronoun.
25.grammar: A noun with a possessor pronoun. The -i ending is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to another noun ('after… OF their fear'); the suffix -him means 'their' (a group). When -i comes before the pronoun, hum shifts to -him to echo the vowel.

26.meaning: Security, safety, peace of mind — the settled calm of being free from fear. From the same root as īmān (faith) and amāna (trust): what is amn is trustworthy and safe.
26.grammar: A simple noun with the -an ending (tanwīn): the -a marks the accusative case, generally flagging the word as an object of a verb or a complement ('…into security'), and the doubled n-sound makes it indefinite. In writing, this -an often carries a supporting alif.

27.meaning: 'They worship Me' / 'they serve Me' — ʿibāda is devoted service and worship: directing one's obedience, humility, and devotion wholly to its object, with 'Me' attached.
27.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'they' plural: ya- in front, -ūna at the end. Keeping the full -ūna (rather than dropping the nūn) marks the plain ongoing/indicative mood — a statement of what they do. The suffix -nī is 'me'; its n (the 'guarding nūn') cushions the verb before the ī of 'me'.

28.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
28.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

29.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
29.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
29.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

30.meaning: 'In me / with me.' A preposition fused with the first-person singular pronoun, expressing attachment, belief, or trust directed toward the speaker ('me').
30.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī here is the first-person singular object that always follows a preposition or noun; it does not change for case. Combined sense: 'in me' or 'with me.'

31.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
31.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

32.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
32.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

33.meaning: He disbelieved, rejected faith, or was ungrateful. The verb denotes covering over or concealing the truth — refusing to acknowledge what is true, and by extension being ungrateful for a blessing one will not recognize.
33.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he did' the action, viewed as completed. The bare -a ending with no attached subject pronoun signals a single male doer.
33.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve or be ungrateful

34.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
34.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
34.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

35.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
35.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

36.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
36.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

37.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
37.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

38.meaning: Those who defiantly disobey — the active participle 'fāsiq' (one who breaks away from obedience, transgressing moral and religious limits) in its sound masculine plural, with the definite article.
38.grammar: Definite ('al-') sound masculine plural active participle. The '-ūna' ending is the nominative (subject) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence.
38.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away, depart from obedience; to act immorally

1.meaning: And establish / set up / perform fully — a command to make something stand firm and upright, to carry it out properly and consistently (used especially of performing prayer rightly).
1.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something stand/be upright. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to do it.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish

2.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
2.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

3.meaning: And give / hand over / bring — a command to deliver something to someone, to render it to its due recipient.
3.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') joined to a plural command verb of the causative (af'ala) pattern, meaning to make something come to someone, i.e. to give. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee being told to give.
3.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

4.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
4.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
4.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

5.meaning: 'and obey!' — a command to a group to comply, submit to, and follow an order or authority. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …').
5.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all obey!'), joined by 'wa' ('and'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressee in commands.
5.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

6.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
6.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

7.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

7.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

8.meaning: '(that) you may receive mercy / be shown mercy' — to be treated with compassion and mercy by another. Addressed to a group, with the doer of the mercy unnamed.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all are shown mercy' — the subject receives the action rather than doing it). The full '-ūna' ending is the indicative, marking a plain ongoing statement; it often follows a particle expressing hoped-for result ('so that you may be shown mercy').

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: Do (not) suppose / reckon / imagine — to think something to be the case, to deem or assume (often a mistaken estimation).
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The heavy '-anna' ending is the emphatic ('nūn of emphasis'), strengthening the verb — typically attached after a command or prohibition ('do not ever suppose…').
2.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, suppose, estimate

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: Ones who frustrate or escape — those who render another powerless, who thwart, outstrip, or get away beyond reach. 'muʿjizīn' names people who cause incapacity in another, i.e. who escape or cannot be overcome.

parts.en: one who frustrates / escapes (Form IV doer)

5.grammar: An active participle (a noun naming the doer) in the Form IV pattern, 'ones who render [another] unable / who escape'. The '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the case used for objects of verbs, after prepositions, and after certain particles. So it denotes 'those who frustrate/escape' as the object or governed term.
5.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — to be unable, powerless; (Form IV) to render unable, frustrate

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

7.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
7.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

8.meaning: And their refuge / dwelling-place — the place to which they return and where they take shelter or reside. 'Ma'wā' is a place of resort, lodging, or abode.
8.grammar: A noun of place ('place of refuge') ending in a long -ā, whose form does not change for case. The attached -hum(u) means 'their'; the leading wa- means 'and'. The pronoun's vowel appears as -u to ease into a following word.
8.root: ا-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, to lodge, to seek refuge

9.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
9.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

10.meaning: And truly wretched / how evil it is — an exclamation of strong blame. Combines 'and', an emphasis particle, and the frozen verb of dispraise meaning 'what an evil thing!'
10.grammar: 'Wa' is 'and'; 'la-' adds emphasis. 'Biʾsa' is a fixed verb of blame meaning 'how evil/wretched is…', used to condemn something; it does not change form. The fixed -a ending is part of this frozen praise/blame form.

11.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
11.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
11.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Let them ask your permission' — istiʾdhān is the etiquette of seeking leave before entering someone's private space, built on idhn, 'permission' (itself from the word for 'ear': permission is granted by being heard).
4.grammar: Form X verb (istaʾdhana): the sta- element means 'to seek' — to seek idhn, permission. The li- prefix is the 'lām of command', which turns a third-person verb into an instruction: 'let him/them…'. That command-lām puts the verb in the clipped (jussive) mood, ending in a bare consonant; the final -u on -kumu is just a helping vowel to link smoothly into the next word.
4.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; hence hearing, permitting, permission

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

7.meaning: Your (plural) right hands — literally the right hands, used idiomatically for solemn oaths and for lawful possession or authority. With the suffix: 'your right hands'.
7.grammar: A plural noun carrying the nominative -u ending, which typically marks it as the subject (the doer) of a verb. The suffix -kum is the attached possessive pronoun 'your' (plural masculine). The plural can mean 'right hands' or 'oaths', and the phrase 'what your right hands possess' is an idiom for those under one's lawful charge.
7.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune

8.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

9.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

9.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

10.meaning: To reach, attain, arrive at a point or goal — used of arriving at an age, a destination, or a limit.
10.grammar: Present-stem verb, 'they' plural (ya- … -ū). The plural ending appears without its usual final nūn (yablughū, not yablughūna): that dropped nūn is the shortened mood required after particles like lam ('have not yet…') — so the form itself carries a 'not yet reached' or 'that they reach' flavor rather than a plain statement.

11.meaning: Puberty, the age of maturity — literally connected to ḥulm, 'dream': the stage of life marked by the dreams of adolescence, when a child becomes legally responsible.
11.grammar: A definite noun: al- ('the') in front. The final -a is the accusative case, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing reached or attained. With al- attached there is no tanwīn, just the single short vowel.
11.root: ح-ل-م (ḥ-l-m) — dreaming; also maturity and forbearance

12.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
12.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
12.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

13.meaning: "three" — the cardinal number 3.
13.grammar: A cardinal number. The ending -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case; numbers in this construct state precede the thing counted and link to it ("three of …"), with the counted noun following in the genitive. The -a is the case ending shown in the transliteration.

14.meaning: Times, instances, occurrences — the plural of marra, 'one time, once', from the idea of something passing by.
14.grammar: A feminine 'sound' plural: the -āt suffix pluralizes without changing the stem. The -in ending (tanwīn) combines the genitive -i — typically because the word follows a number or another noun in an 'of' relationship ('three OF times') or a preposition — with the doubled-n sound of indefiniteness.

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
16.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
16.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

17.meaning: Ṣalāh — the ritual prayer of Islam: the prescribed act of worship with its standing, bowing, and prostration. The root sense includes connection and devotion; not casual supplication (that is duʿāʾ) but formal, timed worship.
17.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ at the end is the feminine marker). This word's stem is spelled with wāw instead of alif — an archaic Qur'anic orthographic convention for ṣalāh. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a neighboring noun in an 'of' construction ('the prayer OF…') or follows a preposition ('before/at the prayer'). No al- or tanwīn appears because it is made definite by the word it is bound to.

18.meaning: The dawn or daybreak; the moment when the first light splits the darkness of night.
18.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending marks the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or in an 'of'-relationship with a preceding noun.
18.root: ف-ج-ر (f-j-r) — to break/cleave open; the bursting of light at daybreak

19.meaning: A compound meaning 'and at the time / and in the moment of'. It joins the preceding text with 'and', then points to a span or instant of time, presenting it as the circumstance during which something happens.
19.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connector 'and'. The stem ḥīn means a stretch or point of time; its final -a ending is the accusative, which on a time-word commonly works adverbially to mean 'at the time when / during', setting the temporal frame for an action.
19.root: ح-ي-ن (ḥ-y-n) — a span or appointed moment of time

20.meaning: 'You lay aside / put down' — waḍaʿa is to set something down or take it off; with garments, to lay aside one's outer clothes.
20.grammar: Present-tense verb, 'you' plural: ta- prefix plus -ūna ending. The root's first letter (wāw) drops out in the present stem — a regular quirk of wāw-initial verbs (waḍaʿa → taḍaʿūna). Keeping the full -ūna marks the plain indicative mood: a statement of what you habitually do.

21.meaning: Your garments, your clothes — thiyāb is the plural of thawb, a garment or robe; with 'your' attached.
21.grammar: A broken (internal) plural — thawb becomes thiyāb by reshaping the vowels, not by adding a suffix. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, generally marking the word as a verb's object (the thing laid aside, worn, etc.). The suffix -kum is 'your', addressing a group.
21.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — garment; also returning (a garment 'returns' to cover the body)

22.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
22.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

23.meaning: The midday heat, high noon — ẓahīra is the hottest part of the day, the traditional time of the noon rest, related to ẓuhr (noon).
23.grammar: A definite feminine noun: al- ('the') assimilates into the sun-letter ẓ, doubling it in pronunciation (aẓ-ẓahīra). The final -i is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition ('at/from the noon heat') or links the word in an 'of' phrase. The tāʾ before it is the feminine marker.
23.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back; visibility; midday (when the sun is at its height)

24.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
24.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

25.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
25.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
25.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

26.meaning: Ṣalāh — the ritual prayer of Islam: the prescribed act of worship with its standing, bowing, and prostration. The root sense includes connection and devotion; not casual supplication (that is duʿāʾ) but formal, timed worship.
26.grammar: A feminine noun (the tāʾ at the end is the feminine marker). This word's stem is spelled with wāw instead of alif — an archaic Qur'anic orthographic convention for ṣalāh. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a neighboring noun in an 'of' construction ('the prayer OF…') or follows a preposition ('before/at the prayer'). No al- or tanwīn appears because it is made definite by the word it is bound to.

27.meaning: The late evening, nightfall — ʿishāʾ is the period after the twilight fades, and gives its name to the night prayer.
27.grammar: A definite noun with al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as the second half of an 'of' construction ('the prayer OF the night') or as following a preposition. Definite with al-, so no tanwīn — just the single -i.

28.meaning: Three — the cardinal number, often standing at the head of a phrase counting things ('three of…').
28.grammar: A number-noun. The final -u is the nominative case, generally marking the word as the subject or the predicate of a sentence ('…are three'). It carries no tanwīn because a counting word like this typically binds to a following noun in an 'of' relationship ('three OF the times'), which blocks the doubled ending. Arabic numbers 3–10 famously take the opposite gender of the thing counted.

29.meaning: Times or states of privacy and exposure. The singular ʿawra denotes anything private, vulnerable, or improper to expose — the body's private parts, or by extension the private moments of a household when people are undressed or at ease.

parts.en: privacies / vulnerable, private states (plural of ʿawra)

29.grammar: A feminine plural noun (plural of ʿawra). The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: it marks the word as 'a/some' (not 'the'), and the genitive typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
29.root: ع-و-ر (ʿ-w-r) — a weak spot, something exposed or vulnerable

30.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
30.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

31.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
31.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

32.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
32.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

33.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
33.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

34.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
34.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
34.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

35.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — the moral 'weight' of wrongdoing that would settle on someone. Commonly used in the phrase 'there is no junāḥ upon you', i.e. no blame attaches to the act.
35.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative: it marks the word as the subject or main topic of its clause — the thing being affirmed or (very often with this word) denied to exist.
35.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean toward (blame as a 'leaning' away from what is right)

36.meaning: After them — 'after' with an attached pronoun referring to a group of feminine things (such as previously mentioned times or occasions).
36.grammar: Baʿda is a time-word ending in -a, the accusative ending used for adverbs of time ('at the point after…'). The suffix -hunna means 'them' when referring to three or more feminine things, so the whole word means 'after them (fem.)'.
36.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — distance, being after or beyond

37.meaning: Ones who constantly move about or circulate — people who come and go around a place frequently, such as household members and helpers moving freely through a home. The pattern is intensive: not just 'going around' once, but doing so habitually.

parts.en: one who goes around constantly (intensive pattern)

37.grammar: An intensive doer-noun on the faʿʿāl pattern (doubled middle letter = doing something repeatedly or by habit). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative: it signals the word is describing or serving as the subject — 'ones who…'.
37.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle, circulate

38.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
38.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

39.meaning: A phrase meaning 'some of you' or 'one part of you'. It singles out a portion of an addressed group, often paired with 'to/for another' to express a reciprocal relationship within that group.
39.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part/some' carrying the -u ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or doer in its clause. The attached -kum means 'of you all' (plural), so the whole means 'some part of you'.

40.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
40.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

41.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
41.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
41.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

42.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
42.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
42.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

43.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
43.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

44.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
44.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

45.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
45.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

46.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
46.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

47.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
47.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
47.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

48.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
48.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

49.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
49.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
49.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'it reached / attained / arrived at' — to extend to and make contact with a point, person, or limit, whether a message reaching hearers or a thing arriving at its end. It conveys completion of arrival.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it reached'). The plain stem with the final -a marks completed past action and a masculine singular doer.
2.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, convey to its destination

3.meaning: The children — young children collectively; ṭifl is a child, especially one still small and dependent.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- is 'the', and aṭfāl is the broken plural of ṭifl ('child'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of its sentence — the one doing or being something.
3.root: ط-ف-ل (ṭ-f-l) — tenderness, being young and soft; hence a young child

4.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you (plural)'. It points to a portion or selection drawn out of a group of people being addressed.
4.grammar: Built on the preposition min ('from, among, of'). The attached -kum is the plural 'you' pronoun, and its vowel is lengthened to -kumu (instead of the usual -kum) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article. The whole phrase commonly singles out a part of a larger group.

5.meaning: Puberty, the age of maturity — literally connected to ḥulm, 'dream': the stage of life marked by the dreams of adolescence, when a child becomes legally responsible.
5.grammar: A definite noun: al- ('the') in front. The final -a is the accusative case, which generally marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing reached or attained. With al- attached there is no tanwīn, just the single short vowel.
5.root: ح-ل-م (ḥ-l-m) — dreaming; also maturity and forbearance

6.meaning: 'So let them ask permission' — a command that a group must seek leave (permission to enter) before entering. Built on Form X of the root of 'ear/permission': literally 'to seek that one be given leave'.
6.grammar: A commanded verb: fa- means 'so/then', the l- is the 'lām of command' turning the verb into 'let them…', ya- plus the plural -ū ending means 'they (a group of men, or mixed group)'. The stem is Form X (ista-), whose sense is 'to seek or ask for' the root idea — here, to seek leave/permission.
6.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — the ear; hence to give ear, grant leave, permit

7.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
7.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

8.meaning: 'He asked permission' / 'sought leave' — the completed act of requesting permission before entering or acting, from the same 'seek leave' verb.
8.grammar: A Form X past-tense verb. The ista- prefix means 'to seek/ask for' the root idea (permission). The final -a vowel is the standard past-tense ending for 'he': the action is complete and its doer is a masculine singular ('he asked permission').
8.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — the ear; to give ear, grant leave, permit

9.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
9.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
11.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

12.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
12.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
12.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

13.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
13.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: 'For you / to you (plural)' — the preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to') joined to the attached pronoun for a group being addressed.
15.grammar: li- is a preposition meaning 'for/to'; its vowel appears here as 'la' before the attached pronoun. The -kum ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'you', so the whole means 'for you (all)'.

16.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
16.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
16.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

17.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
17.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
17.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

18.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

19.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
19.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
19.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'And the women who sit' — qawāʿid (plural of qāʿid) literally means 'those who sit/stay seated', used of elderly women past childbearing who no longer expect marriage; they have 'sat down' from that stage of life.
1.grammar: Wa- is the ordinary connector 'and'; al- is 'the'. Qawāʿid is a broken plural of the doer-noun qāʿid ('one who sits'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which generally marks the word as the subject — the ones about whom something is stated.
1.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, stay put, settle down

2.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
2.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

3.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
3.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

4.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
4.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: They hold out hope for something, expecting and longing for a good outcome (often divine reward or mercy). The verb can carry both hoping for good and, in some contexts, fearing/anticipating.
6.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending is the indicative form, signalling a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hope / they keep hoping').

7.meaning: Marriage — the marriage contract and union itself; nikāḥ is the formal bond of wedlock.
7.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb or as the thing hoped for, done, or aimed at — 'a marriage' as the target of the action.

8.meaning: Then he/it is not; a negation that denies a present state or quality — 'is not the case', 'is not so'. The base word laysa specifically negates being or existence in the present.
8.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem laysa is a special negating verb meaning 'is not', used to deny a present state. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it is not').
8.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation of being; 'is not' (defective verb)

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them (a group of females).' It places a duty, burden, or claim 'on' a group of women — what is incumbent upon or held against them.
9.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- when an attached pronoun follows, often conveying obligation or something weighing upon someone. The suffix -hinna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun 'them,' for a group of females; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

10.meaning: Blame, fault, or sin incurred by an action; a moral lapse for which one is held accountable. In Qur'anic usage it most often appears in the phrase 'there is no junāḥ', i.e. no blame or wrongdoing attaches to doing something.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nominative case with nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a blame / any sin') and signals that it functions as a subject or the noun of existence ('there is a …'). The nunation (the -n sound) is the mark of indefiniteness.
10.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline or lean away (hence to deviate toward wrongdoing; the root also yields 'wing' and 'side')

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: They (a group of women) lay down or deliver — the verb waḍaʿa means to set something down, and of an expectant mother it means to give birth, to be delivered of what she carries.
12.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb. The ya- prefix marks the imperfect tense, and the -na ending marks a feminine plural subject: 'they (women) do/will do'. Verbs with this feminine-plural -na keep the same form in every mood, so the ending stays -na regardless of surrounding particles.
12.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to put down, set, deliver

13.meaning: 'Their garments' — thiyāb is the plural of thawb, a garment or piece of clothing, especially the outer wrap worn over one's ordinary clothes; with 'their (women's)' attached.
13.grammar: A plural noun with two attachments: the -a is the accusative case ending, which usually marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted on — e.g. put down, taken off). The suffix -hunna means 'their' for a group of three or more women.
13.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — to return; a garment is what one keeps returning to and putting on

14.meaning: 'Other than / different from / not'. A noun used to express difference or negation — 'something other than X', and so 'not-X'. It functions to exclude or contrast with what follows.
14.grammar: A noun of difference/exception. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form it takes when it serves as a direct object or as a descriptive substitute standing in an object position; it governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than …'). That it takes case endings and tanwīn confirms it is a true noun, not a particle.
14.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — to be other, different; otherness, change

15.meaning: Women who deliberately display or flaunt their beauty — the Form V participle tabarruj means making one's charms conspicuous, showing off adornment that should be kept private.

parts.en: one who does (Form V doer prefix)

15.grammar: An active participle ('one who does…') of Form V, whose sense is doing something to oneself deliberately — making oneself conspicuous. The -āt suffix marks a feminine plural ('women who…'). The final -in is the indefinite ending which, on -āt plurals, serves for both the object case and the genitive — it signals 'not being the subject' of the clause.
15.root: ب-ر-ج (b-r-j) — a tower, something raised and conspicuous; hence to show oneself off

16.meaning: 'With adornment' — zīna is beautification: ornaments, finery, anything by which a person or thing is made attractive; preceded by 'with/by'.
16.grammar: The prefix bi- is the preposition 'with/by', and every noun after a preposition takes the genitive — hence the -in ending, the indefinite genitive ('with [some] adornment'). The -t- heard before the ending is the feminine marker (tāʾ marbūṭa) pronounced when an ending follows.
16.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, beautify

17.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
17.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

18.meaning: 'They (women) restrain themselves modestly' — Form X of ʿiffa (chastity, self-restraint): to actively seek and hold to modest self-restraint, choosing the more chaste course even when an allowance exists.

parts.en: seek chastity / hold to restraint (Form X stem)

18.grammar: A present-tense verb: ya- marks the present/ongoing tense, and the -na ending means the doers are 'they' — a group of three or more women. The stem is Form X (ista-), 'to seek for oneself' the root idea: to pursue chastity and self-restraint deliberately.
18.root: ع-ف-ف (ʿ-f-f) — chastity, restraint, holding back from what is unbecoming

19.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
19.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
19.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

20.meaning: 'For them / belonging to them' — the preposition 'for, to' joined to the pronoun for a group of females, expressing benefit, possession, or belonging directed toward them.
20.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hunna ('them,' a group of females). When this pronoun is attached, the preposition is vowelled la-. It expresses benefit or possession ('for them, theirs').

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: All-Hearing / ever-hearing — one who hears completely and perfectly, missing nothing of what is uttered or whispered; an intensive form stressing the fullness of the quality. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a constant, perfect quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is all-hearing").

23.meaning: 'All-Knowing / deeply knowledgeable' — an intensive adjective from the root for knowledge, describing one whose knowledge is vast and complete; when applied in the highest sense it means perfectly and comprehensively knowing all things.
23.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun of the 'faʿīl' pattern, expressing an abundant, deep-seated quality ('one who knows thoroughly'). The final -un is the nominative case with 'tanwīn' (nunation) and indefiniteness — the nominative is the basic 'subject / predicate' state, and the doubled-n sound marks it as indefinite ('(an) all-knowing one').

1.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.

Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

2.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').

It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).

3.meaning: 'The blind one' — a person lacking sight. Often used figuratively for one who cannot perceive truth or guidance.
3.grammar: A definite descriptive noun/adjective ('the blind') marked by 'al-' ('the'), built on the pattern used for colours and bodily traits. It ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel and does not change its ending for case — the form stays the same whether subject or object.
3.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight or insight

15.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
15.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
16.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
16.root: — (particle; no root)

17.meaning: '(that) you eat / consume' — to take in food, and by extension to devour or consume wealth or property. Addressed to a group ('you all').
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The plural '-ū' ending (without the usual final '-na') shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive — typically after a particle of purpose, negation, or prohibition ('that you (not) eat').

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: Your houses — dwellings or homes belonging to a group of people.
19.grammar: The plural noun 'houses' in construct (possessive) with the attached pronoun -kum, 'your (all)'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive case, which fits because the word follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun and is being possessed ('… of your houses / in your houses').
19.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, dwelling; to spend the night

20.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
20.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

45.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
45.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

46.meaning: 'You (all) possess' or 'have come to own' — the verb malaka means to own, possess, or have rightful control over something; here completed action with a plural 'you' as its doer.
46.grammar: A past-tense verb: the stem malak- carries the meaning 'own/possess', and the ending -tum means the doers are 'you (a group)' — the standard past-tense ending for addressing several people. Past tense in Arabic marks a completed action or an established fact.
46.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, have dominion (the same root as malik, 'king')

47.grammar: A plural noun with two attachments: the -a is the accusative case ending, which usually marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing possessed, held, etc.). 49.meaning: Your friend — a true, sincere companion. The word ṣadīq is an intensive form built on the idea of truthfulness: a friend whose loyalty and affection are proven genuine.
49.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -kum, 'your' addressed to a group. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to another noun ('… of …').

51.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
51.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

52.meaning: Blame, fault, or sin incurred by an action; a moral lapse for which one is held accountable. In Qur'anic usage it most often appears in the phrase 'there is no junāḥ', i.e. no blame or wrongdoing attaches to doing something.
52.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nominative case with nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a blame / any sin') and signals that it functions as a subject or the noun of existence ('there is a …'). The nunation (the -n sound) is the mark of indefiniteness.
52.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline or lean away (hence to deviate toward wrongdoing; the root also yields 'wing' and 'side')

55.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
55.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

56.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.

57.meaning: Separately, in scattered or separate groups — the plural of a word meaning 'dispersed thing', used adverbially: doing something apart from one another rather than together.
57.grammar: A plural noun with the indefinite accusative ending -an. This ending often turns a noun into an adverb of manner or state — 'in a … way / as …' — so the word as a whole means '(acting) in separate groups, apart from one another'.

58.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
58.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

59.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) entered' or 'you went in.' The core sense is entering or going into something; idiomatically the root can imply intimacy or consummation when paired with a person.
59.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as 'you' for a group of males or a mixed group, indicating a completed action they performed. The suffix both names the doer and signals that the event is finished.

60.meaning: Homes / houses — dwelling places where people live and shelter; the plural of 'bayt' (house). Marked as indefinite ('homes' rather than 'the homes').
60.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an (tanwīn with alif) marks it indefinite and accusative — the case for a direct object or, as often with such forms, a noun expressing purpose or result ('as homes'). It signals 'houses/homes' indefinitely, not 'the houses'.
60.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night, lodge; hence 'bayt', a house/dwelling

61.meaning: 'Then greet (with peace)' — a command to a group to offer the greeting of salām, invoking peace and well-being upon those greeted (or upon oneself).
61.grammar: fa- means 'so/then', linking the command to what precedes it. The verb is an intensive (Form II) imperative; the -ū ending marks it as a command addressed to a group: 'you all, greet!'
