64.meaning: A greeting — taḥiyya is the act of greeting someone with a wish for their life and wellbeing (from the same root as ḥayāh, 'life'); a salutation of peace and welcome.

parts.en: greeting, salutation of life and peace

64.grammar: A verbal noun naming the act of greeting. The -an accusative ending with nunation typically marks what is given or the thing an action is done with ('received WITH a greeting'), and marks the word as indefinite — 'a greeting'.

65.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
65.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

66.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
66.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
66.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

67.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
67.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

68.meaning: Blessed — carrying divine blessing (baraka): endowed with goodness that is abundant, growing, and lasting.
68.grammar: A passive participle ('one that has been blessed'). The -at ending makes it feminine, agreeing with a feminine noun it describes; the final -an is the indefinite accusative ending, the case used for direct objects and descriptions of state.

69.meaning: An adjective meaning 'good', 'pure', or 'wholesome' (describing a feminine noun) — that which is fine, sound, agreeable, and untainted, whether in substance, character, or speech.
69.grammar: A feminine singular adjective ('good / pure'). The final -tan ending combines the feminine marker with 'tanwīn' (the -n sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a …') in the accusative case, which typically marks it as a direct object or describes such a noun.

70.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
70.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
70.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

71.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
71.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

72.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
72.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

73.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
73.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

74.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
74.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

75.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

75.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

76.meaning: 'You understand / use reason' — to comprehend, think, and grasp matters with the intellect; to apply sound reasoning.
76.grammar: The prefix 'ta-' marks a 2nd-person present-tense verb, and the '-ūna' ending makes the subject a masculine-inclusive plural 'you all.' The '-ūna' is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual or ongoing statement.
76.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to reason, understand, be intelligent

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
2.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
6.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

7.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
9.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
10.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

11.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or decree. The word spans two senses from one root: an ordered 'command' and the 'affair/situation' that results from it. The indefinite form points to 'some matter' or 'a decision' in general.
11.grammar: A noun in the genitive state with tanwīn (the -in ending), marking it as indefinite ('a matter') and governed either by a preceding preposition or by being joined to a foregoing noun ('… of a matter').
11.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; also matter, affair

12.meaning: Gathering, uniting, collective — an active participle meaning 'that which brings together', used of a matter or occasion that assembles people as one body.
12.grammar: An active participle ('doing the gathering'). The -in ending is the indefinite genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of an '… of …' phrase, and the case an adjective takes when it agrees with a genitive noun it describes.

13.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
13.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

14.meaning: 'They go / they leave' — the act of going away or departing, done by a group of people.
14.grammar: The ya- prefix with the -ū ending means 'they (a group of men) go'. Notice the ending is bare -ū, not -ūna: dropping the final -na is the shortened mood a verb takes after certain governing particles (such as 'that', 'not', or 'until'), often giving the sense 'that they may go / do not go'.

15.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
15.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

16.meaning: 'They ask his permission' — a Form X verb meaning to seek someone's leave or authorization before acting, literally 'to request that one be given permission', directed at 'him'.
16.grammar: ya- + -ū marks 'they (plural)'; the attached -hu means 'him', the one whose permission is sought. The plural ending appears as bare -ū without the usual -na, the shortened mood used after governing particles ('until they ask…', 'that they ask…'). The sta- element is the 'seeking' pattern (Form X): to ask for something.
16.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — permission, giving ear, listening

17.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
17.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

18.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
18.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

19.meaning: They ask your permission; they seek leave or authorization from you (a single male addressee). Combines requesting permission with the one asked.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb of the 'seeking' (form X) pattern ('to ask leave'); the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural in the ordinary present ('they ...'), and -ka 'you' is the attached object (one male).
19.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; (form X) to seek permission

20.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
20.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

21.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
21.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

22.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
22.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

23.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
23.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
23.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
24.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
24.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

25.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
25.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

26.meaning: 'They asked your permission' — a completed act of seeking someone's leave, addressed to 'you' (one person): they requested your authorization.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb: the -ū ending means the doers are 'they' (a group), and the attached -ka means 'you' (one male person) as the one asked. The ista- beginning is the 'seeking' pattern (Form X): to request something for oneself.

27.meaning: 'For some (of)' — baʿḍ means 'a part, some portion' of a larger whole; with li- it expresses purpose or benefit: 'for the sake of some…'.
27.grammar: li- is the preposition 'for / for the sake of'. The -i ending is the genitive case, required after a preposition; baʿḍ itself then typically links onwards to a following noun: 'some OF …'.

28.meaning: 'An affair of theirs' — shaʾn is a matter, business, or concern, often one of weight or importance; with the pronoun it means some business belonging to 'them'.
28.grammar: A noun carrying the attached pronoun -him, 'their'. The -i before it is the genitive ending, the case of a noun that follows a preposition or stands in an '… of …' chain.

29.meaning: 'Then give permission' — a command to one person to grant leave, to authorize someone's request.
29.grammar: fa- means 'then/so', tying the command to what came before. The verb is a bare imperative addressed to one man; it ends with no vowel at all (a rest, sukūn), which is exactly how a singular command form ends — the stripped-down stem itself is the order.

30.meaning: It strikes them, it befalls them — used for something, especially a punishment or affliction, reaching or overtaking a group. Masculine form of the same verb as tuṣībahum.

parts.en: it strikes / it befalls (3rd person masculine singular subjunctive)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

30.grammar: The verb is 3rd person masculine singular subjunctive (manṣūb), marked by the -a (fatḥa) ending rather than the indicative -u. The yu- prefix indicates masculine third person (the subject is a masculine noun — such as ʿadhāb, 'punishment'). The subjunctive is required by the surrounding grammatical context (following a particle or conditional construction). The attached -hum is the 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun ('them').
30.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to strike, to hit, to befall, to be correct

31.meaning: You willed / you wished — you chose and intended something to be. The verb expresses an act of will and desire on the part of the one addressed.
31.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the subject suffix -ta meaning 'you' (a single male addressee). It reports a completed act of willing.
31.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish; the root behind 'thing'

32.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
32.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

33.meaning: A command meaning 'and seek forgiveness' — an appeal to Allah to cover, pardon, and protect one from the consequences of sin. The verb conveys actively asking for that pardon, not merely wishing for it.
33.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'do (you) seek forgiveness.' The form built on the ist- pattern conveys 'to ask/seek for' something, so it means 'request forgiveness.' The bare ending with no final vowel marks it as a direct order. The wa- prefix simply links it to what precedes as 'and.'

34.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
34.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

35.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
35.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

36.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
36.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

37.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
37.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

38.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
38.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.

39.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
39.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
1.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

2.meaning: A verb addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'you (all) make', 'you set up', 'you place', or 'you render (something into something).' The verb jaʿala carries the sense of making, forming, or appointing.

parts.en: plural 'you all' (and, after a prohibition particle, the cut-off mood)

2.grammar: The 'ta-' prefix marks a present/future verb addressed to 'you'. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('you all'). The dropping of the final 'n' (jussive/subjunctive form) is what a preceding particle like 'lā' of prohibition triggers, turning it into 'do not do …'.
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to render

3.meaning: The calling — a verbal noun covering calling out, summoning, inviting, and supplicating; the act of addressing someone to draw their attention or response.
3.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of calling'). The final -a is the accusative ending, the case a noun typically takes as the object of a verb ('do not make the calling…') or in similar constructions; the bare -a with no -n shows it is linked to a following word ('the calling OF …').

4.meaning: the Messenger — one sent with a message; specifically an envoy commissioned by Allah to convey His revelation. 'Rasūl' is a faʿūl-pattern noun denoting the one who is sent.
4.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') is assimilated into the 'sun letter' r (so it sounds ar-r). The ending -i marks the genitive case, the form a word typically takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, an envoy

5.meaning: Between you / among you; the space or relation linking the members of a group.
5.grammar: An adverb of place ('between/among') with an attached pronoun. The fixed -a ending is characteristic of such place-words; the ending -kum means 'you' for a group, so the whole means 'among you all'.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation/interval; the space between two things

6.meaning: 'Like the calling of' — the same word duʿāʾ (calling, summoning) preceded by the comparison particle ka-: 'in the manner of the call of…'.
6.grammar: ka- is the preposition of comparison, 'like/as'. The -i ending is the genitive case that a noun must take after such a particle, and it also points forward: 'like the calling OF (someone)'.

7.meaning: (of) some of you
7.grammar: See full Arabic lexicon for detailed grammatical analysis.

8.meaning: Some, a part, or one of a group — 'another' when paired with 'one'. It singles out an unspecified portion or member set against the rest.

parts.en: some / a part / one (of a group)

8.grammar: A noun meaning 'a part / some'. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case used for a direct object. Paired with baʿḍ ('another'), it builds the sense 'one another / each other'.
8.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, a portion, some of a whole

9.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

10.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
10.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: 'They slip away stealthily' — a Form V verb picturing people stealing off quietly one by one, drawing themselves out of a gathering unnoticed, like a thing gently drawn from its sheath.
13.grammar: ya- plus the full ending -ūna marks 'they (a group) do it' in the normal present tense: the -na is kept because no particle governs the verb, so it describes an actual ongoing or habitual action.

14.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
14.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
14.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

15.meaning: Taking cover — a verbal noun of 'seeking shelter behind something': screening oneself behind another person or object so as not to be seen; used adverbially, 'shielding one behind another'.
15.grammar: A verbal noun with the indefinite accusative ending -an, which typically makes the noun describe the manner or state of an action: '(doing something) while taking cover'. Note that the li- belongs to the word's own root (l-w-dh); it is not the preposition 'for'.

16.meaning: 'So let him beware' — a third-person command built with the 'lām of command': an order that 'he' (whoever is meant) be on his guard, take warning, and fear the consequences.
16.grammar: fa- means 'so', and the little l- is the 'lām of command', which turns a 'he does' verb into 'let him do'. A verb commanded this way normally ends in silence (no vowel, sukūn); when such a form is vocalized with a final -i, that is merely a helping vowel of the kind Arabic inserts to keep an unvowelled ending from colliding with what is joined to it in connected speech — it is purely phonetic and does not change the command mood.
16.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — caution, wariness, being on guard

17.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
17.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

18.meaning: 'They go against / oppose' — a Form III verb meaning to act contrary to someone or something, to deviate from and contravene it; from the idea of turning to what lies 'behind' instead of following.
18.grammar: yu- with the full ending -ūna means 'they do it' in the plain present tense; keeping the final -na shows the verb is ungoverned by any particle, describing a real, ongoing or habitual behavior.

19.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

19.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

20.meaning: 'His command' — amr means an order or decree, and more broadly a matter or affair; with the pronoun it is the command or business belonging to 'him'.
20.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hi, 'his'. The -i before the pronoun is the genitive ending, the case of a noun that follows a preposition or completes an '… of …' construction; the pronoun itself is pronounced -hi (rather than -hu) simply to echo that i-sound.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

22.meaning: struck them / afflicted them / reached them. Refers to something befalling people — a calamity or divine punishment reaching and affecting a group.

parts.en: it strikes, it befalls, it afflicts (Form IV subjunctive)

22.grammar: Present-tense verb, subjunctive mood (manṣūb), 3rd person feminine singular, Form IV (aṣāba — to strike, to afflict). The -a ending marks subjunctive; -hum is the plural object pronoun.
22.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark; Form IV: to strike, to afflict, to befall

23.meaning: A trial, test, or tribulation. Fitna originally meant smelting gold in fire to test its purity — so it is any ordeal, temptation, or upheaval that puts what a person is really made of to the proof.
23.grammar: A feminine noun (the -a(t) of the stem is the feminine marker). The -un part of the ending is the nominative case — the form a noun takes when it is the subject or the one doing/being something — and the final -n (tanwīn) marks it indefinite: 'a trial', not a specific named one.
23.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — testing by fire, trial, temptation

24.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
24.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

25.meaning: '(That) He may strike / afflict / befall them' — a verb meaning to hit the mark or let something reach and touch someone, often of a calamity or decree landing upon a group, with 'He' as the one who brings it and 'them' as those reached.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to cause to reach/hit'). The yu- prefix marks 'he'. The -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after particles of purpose or intent ('so that He may …'). The attached -hum is the object 'them' — those struck or reached.
25.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, reach, befall correctly

26.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
26.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

27.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
27.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
1.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

2.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
2.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
6.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

7.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
7.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

8.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

9.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

10.meaning: A word meaning 'what' or 'that which' — a relative/indefinite particle pointing to an unspecified thing ('what', 'whatever', 'that which').
10.grammar: An invariable particle (mā) with no case ending. Depending on context it works as a relative pronoun ('that which') introducing a clause, or as an interrogative/indefinite ('what'). It does not inflect for case, gender, or number.

11.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
11.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

12.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
12.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

13.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
13.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

14.meaning: 'They are returned / brought back.' A passive form: the subjects do not act but are themselves caused to return to someone, conveying that all will ultimately be brought back to Allah.
14.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The vowel pattern (yu-…-a-) makes it passive: the subject is acted upon ('are returned') rather than acting. The -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood used for plain statements.
14.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, bring back

15.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

16.meaning: so He will then inform them / announce to them the truth of a matter. The 'so/then' prefix joins to a verb meaning to give weighty news or notify, with an attached 'them.' The doubled-letter stem suggests full, emphatic disclosure.
16.grammar: A present/imperfect verb on an intensive doubled-letter pattern (to inform fully). The prefix yu- marks a single male subject 'he,' and the final -u vowel on the stem signals the plain indicative mood (a straightforward statement, 'he informs'). The attached -hum is the object 'them.' The fa- prefix means 'so/then.'
16.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — weighty news, tidings; to inform, announce

17.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
17.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

18.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
18.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
18.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

19.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
19.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
19.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

20.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
20.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
